title: A rapid and simple method to quantify per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in plasma and serum using 96-well plates
author: Da Silva, Ahmadireskety, et al.
materials: PFAS analyses were executed using a Thermo Scientific Vanquish UHPLC coupled to a TSQ Quantis triple quadrupole mass spectrometer. Chromatographic separation was achieved using a Gemini C18 column (100 mm x 2 mm; 3 µm) from Phenomenex (Torrence, CA, USA). The UHPLC was fitted with a Vanquish PFAS Replacement Kit, among which included an Acclaim™ 120 C18 (2.1 × 50 mm, 5 µm, 120 Å) as a delay column and UHPLC PFAS-free plumbing and hardware to minimize PFAS background. Water [A] and methanol [B] both containing 5 mM ammonium acetate, were used as the mobile phases. The gradient elution was set as follows: 0–3 min 10% B, 3–4.5 min 10–35% B, 4.5–12.5 min 35–95% B, 12.5–12.51 min 95–99% B, 12.51–19 min 99% and then equilibrated back to initial conditions in 30 min. The autosampler temperature was set to 4 °C and the flow rate and injection volume were set to 0.5 mL.min−1 and 10 µL, respectively. Selected-reaction monitoring (SRM) transitions were used to detect and quantify PFAS, with the most intense transition used to quantify the compounds while the second transition was used to confirm identification (if applicable). Table S3 shows all PFAS transitions and additional parameters used for these experiments. Source parameters (in negative mode) were set as follows: ion spray voltage −1500 V and sheath and auxiliary gas set to 50 and 10 arb, respectively. Ion transfer tube temperature was set at 250 °C while the vaporizer temperature was set to 550 °C. Data acquisition and peak integration were performed using Xcalibur v.4.1 software (Thermo Fisher Scientific).

steps.title: Rinse 96‑well plate with methanol
steps.instruction: Rinse each 96‑well collection plate three times with Optima‑grade methanol before any sample processing.

steps.title: Add sample and internal standard
steps.instruction: Dispense 100 µL of plasma, serum, or Optima‑grade water (for blanks) into each well; add 20 µL of the isotope‑labeled internal‑standard mixture to all wells except blank wells.

steps.title: Mix plate gently
steps.instruction: Place the plate on a Fisher microplate vortexer and mix gently for 5 min at 400 rpm.

steps.title: Add methanol crash solvent
steps.instruction: Add 380 µL of Optima‑grade methanol to each well containing sample (giving a 4:1 solvent‑to‑sample ratio). For wells that will be spiked post‑extraction, add 400 µL methanol so that the final volume reaches 500 µL.

steps.title: Vortex plate
steps.instruction: Vortex the plate for 5 min at 450 rpm to ensure thorough protein precipitation.

steps.title: Centrifuge plate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate for 15 min at 400 × g to pellet precipitated proteins.

steps.title: Place micromat and load autosampler
steps.instruction: Place a micromat onto the plate to separate the supernatant, then seat the entire plate directly in the Vanquish UHPLC autosampler; set the injection depth to 5 mm and the autosampler temperature to 4 °C.

steps.title: Set UHPLC‑MS/MS conditions
steps.instruction: Configure the UHPLC‑MS/MS system as follows: use a Gemini C18 column (100 mm × 2 mm, 3 µm) with a PFAS Replacement Kit (delay column Acclaim™ 120 C18, 2.1 × 50 mm, 5 µm, 120 Å); mobile phase A = water with 5 mM ammonium acetate, mobile phase B = methanol with 5 mM ammonium acetate; flow rate 0.5 mL·min⁻¹, injection volume 10 µL; gradient: 0–3 min 10 % B, 3–4.5 min 10–35 % B, 4.5–12.5 min 35–95 % B, 12.5–12.51 min 95–99 % B, 12.51–19 min 99 % B, then re‑equilibrate to initial conditions by 30 min total; source (negative mode) voltage –1500 V, sheath gas 50 arb, auxiliary gas 10 arb, ion‑transfer tube 250 °C, vaporizer 550 °C; autosampler temperature 4 °C.

steps.title: Run UHPLC gradient and MS acquisition
steps.instruction: Start the UHPLC run using the gradient above; acquire data in selected‑reaction monitoring (SRM) mode, using the most intense transition for quantification and a second transition for confirmation for each PFAS.

steps.title: Perform data integration and quantification
steps.instruction: Integrate the quantifier peak for each PFAS in Xcalibur v4.1; sum isomeric peaks for PFHxS and PFOS (ΣPFHxS, ΣPFOS); for analytes lacking a labeled analogue, use the closest internal standard by retention time; generate calibration curves (200 µL of each level added to 96‑well plates) and calculate slope, intercept, R², LOD (S/N ≥ 3, <20 % RSD, n = 7) and LOQ (S/N ≥ 10, <20 % RSD); compute extraction recovery as the ratio of pre‑spike to post‑spike peak areas (%), and assess precision (RSD) and accuracy from QC samples.

steps.title: Conduct extraction efficiency experiment
steps.instruction: In six wells add 100 µL in‑house plasma pool; spike three wells with 20 µL IS before extraction and three wells after extraction; add 380 µL methanol to pre‑spiked wells and 400 µL methanol to post‑spiked wells (final volume 500 µL); process as per steps 3–7 and compare peak areas to determine recovery (average ~82 % for plasma, ~94 % for water).

steps.title: Perform blank extraction for background check
steps.instruction: Designate three wells as blanks; add 100 µL Optima‑grade water and 400 µL methanol (no IS); process through steps 3–7; analyze to identify any PFAS background (e.g., 6:2 FTS detected and excluded from quantitation).

steps.title: Prepare QC samples and calibration standards
steps.instruction: Prepare low‑level QC (0.08 ng·mL⁻¹) and mid‑level QC (0.8 ng·mL⁻¹) by spiking water with non‑labeled PFAS; add internal standard solution; run each QC in triplicate over three days; also prepare calibration standards by adding 200 µL of each concentration level to separate wells of a 96‑well plate.
